subject.title: [Feature]: WebUI notification system, cron job management popups, and context monitor integration

question: Should Control UI context pressure and cron completion results use a shared in-app notification queue, or should context pressure remain inline while only cron/admin events use popups?
rationale: The remaining behavior is not a narrow missing bug; it requires choosing notification ownership, action semantics, and overlap with related UI action-surface issues.

options.title: Split and keep canonical tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open as the broad tracker, then spawn or bless narrower work for notification queue, cron snooze, and context-pressure UX.

options.title: Cron-only first
options.body: Limit the first implementation to cron finished popups and snooze/reschedule, leaving context pressure inline until a later notification policy is approved.

options.title: Defer notification architecture
options.body: Leave current inline context and cron management in place and wait for the narrower admin notification or inline-button surfaces to settle first.

recommendation.title: Split and keep canonical tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the broad tracker, then spawn or bless narrower work for notification queue, cron snooze, and context-pressure UX.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent cron UI/runtime history and already carried a prior review of the remaining scope in the issue discussion.
